app.notes: Blockbench 5.2.2 web app (the same build as web.blockbench.net) built with `npm run build-web` (esbuild) and assembled into .ui-capture/out by .ui-capture/build_out.sh (index.html, dist/bundle.js, css, assets, font, lib, content). The front end needs no backend. Tooling: node 24.22.3 via mise.toml (matches CI). Data: Blockbench web keeps its user state in the browser, so .ui-capture/seed/seed_loader.js (a separate classic script injected before the bundle in out/index.html) seeds it on first load from out/seed/*.json, which .ui-capture/seed/generate.mjs produces: (1) localStorage settings of a long-time user (username 'mossbyte', ~148 launches, custom palette and color history, recently used actions); (2) the IndexedDB 'auto_backups' store that Blockbench uses for project recovery, holding 6 projects in the native .bbmodel 5.0 format (146 cubes, 14 animations total, each with editor_state: camera, selected element, saved flag) with generated pixel-art textures: red_panda (Bedrock entity, 15 cubes, 5 animations incl. a WIP climb), goblin_merchant (Bedrock entity with backpack/lantern/wares, 5 animations), sky_skiff_mk2 (Generic model airship, 76 cubes, 3 animations), copper_lantern_post (Java block, 4 textures, display transforms), mossy_mushroom_stool (Java block), ember_wisp (small Bedrock entity). After the app boots, the loader opens them with Blockbench's own AutoBackup.recoverAllBackups() (the 'Recover' action on the start screen) and focuses red_panda, so the editor opens with six project tabs. Open /?start to land on the start screen instead (it shows the 'Recover backup' banner plus model format list). Main areas: menu bar, project tabs, Edit/Paint/Animate modes (toolbar top right), 3D viewport, UV editor + Textures panel (left), Transform/Element and Outliner panels (right), Animate mode timeline/animations list, Display mode (Java block models), File > Plugins (store backed by the stub catalog), Settings, Keybindings. The browser needs WebGL. Rebuild everything with .ui-capture/build_out.sh; .ui-capture/tools/check.mjs is the headless screenshot check used during setup (serves out/ on :5471). The only console error is the app trying to register ./service_worker.js, which the web build does not produce without `npm run pwa`; it is harmless.

# Running it

# Tools: use mise
Install every runtime and tool you need (node, the package manager, python, bun, ...) with mise, pinned to exact versions in a mise.toml at the repo root, so the setup can be reproduced. Match what the repo asks for (engines, .nvmrc, .tool-versions, packageManager). mise is already configured for this directory: `mise install` installs into ./.ui-capture/mise, and its shims come first on PATH, so `node`, `pnpm` and the rest resolve to the pinned versions. Don't use other copies of these tools or download runtimes by hand.

# Secrets, API keys and external services: fake them
The app must not depend on anything outside this machine, and when it runs it has no network except localhost. Wherever it expects secrets, environment variables, API keys or third-party services (hosted auth or OAuth, payment providers, email, LLM or other AI APIs, maps, storage buckets, analytics, hosted databases):

Keep stubs out of UI code. Responses should look like what the real service returns for a real user, e.g. an AI reply that actually answers, a payment history with real-looking amounts.

List every stub in app.json.

# Data: like real use
Seed it the way an established user's data would look after months of actual use: specific, plausible names and content for this kind of app; dates spread over time; a realistic mix of states (done, in progress, overdue, archived, ...); realistic volume (dozens to hundreds of records where the app revolves around records); short and long text; some messiness real data has. Start from the app's own demo or seed data if it has realistic data, and extend it if it's thin. Load data through the app's own paths (its API, import, seed scripts, or its database schema), never by hardcoding it into UI code. If the app needs an account, create one and attach the data to it. You have 90 minutes in total, and anything unfinished when time runs out is lost. So work in this order:
